topics.label: Boolean Algebra
topics.desc: Algebra of logic over {0,1} with AND/OR/NOT that formalizes circuit behavior and underpins all gate-level design and simplification.

topics.label: Logic Gates
topics.desc: Physical primitives (NAND, NOR, XOR) realizing Boolean functions; NAND/NOR are functionally complete, so all logic reduces to them.

topics.label: Combinational Logic
topics.desc: Stateless circuits whose outputs depend only on current inputs, built from gates into adders, multiplexers, decoders, and ALUs.

topics.label: Sequential Logic
topics.desc: Circuits with memory whose output depends on input and stored state, enabling counters, registers, and finite-state machines.

topics.label: Flip-Flops & Latches
topics.desc: Bistable storage elements (SR, D, JK) that hold a single bit and form the building blocks of registers and synchronous memory.

topics.label: Karnaugh Maps
topics.desc: Graphical method for minimizing Boolean expressions by grouping adjacent minterms, reducing gate count in small combinational designs.

topics.label: Number Representation
topics.desc: Binary, hex, two's-complement, and IEEE-754 encodings defining how integers and reals are stored and how arithmetic overflow behaves.

topics.label: Von Neumann Architecture
topics.desc: Stored-program model with unified memory for code and data, defining the fetch-decode-execute cycle and the von Neumann bottleneck.

topics.label: Instruction Set Architecture
topics.desc: The hardware-software contract specifying registers, instructions, and memory model; the abstraction compilers target and CPUs implement.

topics.label: RISC vs CISC
topics.desc: Contrasting ISA philosophies: fixed-length simple instructions (RISC, e.g. ARM/RISC-V) versus rich variable-length ones (CISC, e.g. x86).

topics.label: Datapath & Control Unit
topics.desc: The execution core — ALU, registers, buses — steered by a hardwired or microcoded control unit that sequences each instruction.

topics.label: Pipelining
topics.desc: Overlapping instruction stages (fetch, decode, execute, memory, writeback) to raise throughput, bounded by hazards and stalls.

topics.label: Branch Prediction
topics.desc: Speculating control flow to keep deep pipelines fed; mispredicts flush the pipeline and dominate the cost of unpredictable branches.

topics.label: Superscalar & OoO Execution
topics.desc: Issuing multiple instructions per cycle and executing out of program order via register renaming and reorder buffers to extract ILP.

topics.label: SIMD & Vector Units
topics.desc: Data-parallel execution applying one instruction to many lanes (SSE/AVX/NEON), key to throughput in media, ML, and numerical kernels.

topics.label: Memory Hierarchy
topics.desc: Layered storage from registers to disk trading speed for capacity, exploiting locality so most accesses hit fast, small upper levels.

topics.label: CPU Caches
topics.desc: Small fast SRAM holding recently used lines to hide DRAM latency; the single biggest lever on real-world program performance.

topics.label: Cache Associativity
topics.desc: How lines map to sets — direct-mapped, set-associative, or fully associative — trading hit rate against lookup cost and conflict misses.

topics.label: Cache Coherence
topics.desc: Protocols (MESI/MOESI) keeping per-core caches consistent in multiprocessors, the source of false-sharing and cache-line ping-pong.

topics.label: Locality of Reference
topics.desc: The empirical tendency of programs to reuse nearby addresses in time and space, the principle that makes caching effective at all.

topics.label: Virtual Memory
topics.desc: Per-process address spaces mapped to physical frames via page tables, giving isolation, protection, and demand paging from disk.

topics.label: TLB
topics.desc: A cache of recent virtual-to-physical translations; misses trigger costly page-table walks, making TLB pressure a real performance factor.

topics.label: Machine Code
topics.desc: The binary instruction encoding a CPU executes directly, into which assembly mnemonics and ultimately all compiled programs are translated.

topics.label: Assembly Language
topics.desc: Human-readable mnemonics mapping nearly one-to-one to machine instructions, essential for low-level debugging, reversing, and hot-path tuning.

topics.label: Registers & Addressing Modes
topics.desc: The CPU's fast named storage and the ways operands are located (immediate, register, indirect, indexed) that shape instruction encoding.

topics.label: Calling Conventions
topics.desc: ABI rules for passing arguments, returning values, and saving registers across calls, enabling separately compiled code to interoperate.

topics.label: Stack & Stack Frames
topics.desc: Per-call activation records holding locals, saved registers, and return addresses; the structure exploited by stack-overflow attacks.

topics.label: Interrupts & Traps
topics.desc: Hardware and software events that divert control to handlers, the mechanism behind I/O notification, system calls, and exceptions.

topics.label: x86 & ARM in Practice
topics.desc: Concrete realities of dominant ISAs — x86-64's CISC quirks and ARM's load-store regularity — that matter when reading real disassembly.

topics.label: Lexical Analysis
topics.desc: Scanning source text into tokens using regular languages and finite automata, the first stage that feeds the parser.

topics.label: Parsing
topics.desc: Building a syntax tree from tokens against a context-free grammar via LL/LR techniques, enforcing the language's structural rules.

topics.label: Context-Free Grammars
topics.desc: Production-rule formalism defining valid program structure, the specification from which parsers and language tooling are derived.

topics.label: Abstract Syntax Trees
topics.desc: A tree stripped of surface syntax representing program structure semantically, the central IR for analysis and transformation.

topics.label: Semantic Analysis
topics.desc: Type checking, name resolution, and scope rules over the AST that catch errors syntax alone cannot, building the symbol table.

topics.label: Symbol Tables & Scoping
topics.desc: Data structures tracking identifiers, types, and visibility across nested scopes, consulted throughout semantic analysis and codegen.

topics.label: Parser Generators
topics.desc: Tools (lex/yacc, ANTLR) that synthesize scanners and parsers from grammar specs, trading control for productivity in language tooling.

topics.label: Intermediate Representation
topics.desc: A language- and target-neutral form (three-address or SSA) bridging front end and back end where most optimization happens.

topics.label: Static Single Assignment
topics.desc: An IR where each variable is assigned once, with phi-nodes at merges, making dataflow optimizations dramatically simpler and faster.

topics.label: Optimization Passes
topics.desc: Semantics-preserving IR transforms — constant folding, dead-code elimination, CSE, loop opts — that improve speed or size.

topics.label: Dataflow Analysis
topics.desc: Fixpoint computation of facts (liveness, reaching definitions) over the control-flow graph that drives most optimization passes.

topics.label: Register Allocation
topics.desc: Assigning unbounded IR values to finite machine registers, classically via graph coloring, spilling to memory when registers run out.

topics.label: Code Generation
topics.desc: Emitting final assembly from optimized IR via instruction selection and scheduling, honoring the target ABI and calling conventions.

topics.label: JIT Compilation
topics.desc: Compiling hot code to native at runtime using profile data, the engine behind JVM, V8, and .NET that beats static guesses.

topics.label: Object Files
topics.desc: Compiler output (ELF, Mach-O, COFF) holding machine code, data, and symbol/relocation tables awaiting linkage into an executable.

topics.label: Static Linking
topics.desc: Combining object files and library archives at build time into one self-contained binary, resolving symbols and applying relocations.

topics.label: Dynamic Linking
topics.desc: Resolving shared-library references at load or runtime via PLT/GOT, saving memory and enabling updates without recompiling callers.

topics.label: Symbol Resolution
topics.desc: Matching undefined references to definitions across objects and libraries, the step where duplicate or missing symbols surface.

topics.label: Relocation
topics.desc: Patching address-dependent fields once final load addresses are known, the mechanism that lets code be placed anywhere in memory.

topics.label: Loaders & Program Startup
topics.desc: OS machinery that maps a binary into memory, sets up the stack, runs the dynamic linker, and jumps to the entry point.

topics.label: Executable Formats
topics.desc: Container layouts (ELF, PE, Mach-O) describing segments, sections, and metadata that loaders and debuggers parse to run a program.

topics.label: Instruction-Level Parallelism
topics.desc: Overlapping independent instructions within a thread, exploited by pipelines and superscalar cores and limited by dependencies.

topics.label: The Memory Wall
topics.desc: The widening gap between CPU and DRAM speed that makes memory latency, not compute, the dominant bottleneck in many workloads.

topics.label: Cache-Aware Optimization
topics.desc: Restructuring data layout and access order (blocking, padding, AoS-vs-SoA) to maximize cache hits and minimize misses.

topics.label: Hardware Performance Counters
topics.desc: On-chip registers exposing cycles, cache misses, and mispredicts that let profilers attribute slowdowns to real microarchitectural events.

topics.label: Roofline Model
topics.desc: A performance bound plotting attainable FLOPS against arithmetic intensity, revealing whether a kernel is compute- or memory-bound.

topics.label: False Sharing
topics.desc: Unrelated variables sharing a cache line causing coherence traffic between cores, a subtle scalability killer fixed by padding/alignment.

topics.label: Amdahl's & Gustafson's Laws
topics.desc: Quantitative limits on speedup from parallelism set by the serial fraction, framing when adding cores actually pays off.
